comments.author: Raythe
comments.body:
This is getting beyond ridiculous. Do some research and shop around a little bit and it becomes really easy to tell who is selling at hyper inflated prices. Don't buy from them, it really is that simple.

the word "scam" is getting thrown around by a lot of people who honestly don't understand or know what that word even means. If you agreed to a price for a certain ship, say a 5/5 MFCV. And you paid exactly what you agreed to pay, and got EXACTLY what you thought you were getting, nobody got scammed. If you overpaid then boohoo for you, do your homework a little better next time.

I never bought any ships from Servicio, in fact the only thing I ever bought from him were Improved Salvage Ropes. They were on the high side, but I knew that when i bought them. Thing is he had them, nobody else did for any cheaper or guess what, I would have bought them elsewhere. I didn't get scammed, I got what I wanted at the price I agreed to.

You guys really need to calm it down a notch and quit calling people out for "scamming" unless they promised you something and delivered something else.

comments.author: Maerlynn
comments.body:
Seconded, Raythe.

I find it especially disturbing that charging a commission is considered "scamming", since it is standard operating procedure in virtually every RL business that involves selling products.

Frankly, if I could pay someone 300 million to go to Seville and sell an item that would net me 1.7 billion, I would do that in a heartbeat, partly because I would rather spend my in-game time playing the game, and partly because (no joke) spending more than ten minutes in Seville can give me an eyestrain headache.

Bottom line: caveat emptor. The only people who get "scammed" are those that agree to bad deals and later found out they could have gotten a better one.
